content: This medication is used to treat women experiencing abnormal uterine bleeding. It is also prescribed for women who have stopped having menstrual periods for several months (a condition known as amenorrhea) but are not pregnant or undergoing menopause. Additionally, it is used to manage endometriosis, a condition where tissue that normally lines the inside of the uterus grows outside the uterus, often in the abdomen or pelvic area, causing painful or irregular periods. Norethindrone is a type of hormone called a progestin, which mimics the natural hormone progesterone produced by the body. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication orally as directed by your doctor. It can be taken with food or after a meal to prevent stomach upset. Follow the prescribed dosing schedule carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor. For the treatment of stopped menstrual periods or abnormal uterine bleeding, this medication is typically taken once daily for 5 to 10 days during the second half of the planned menstrual cycle, as directed by your doctor. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, mood swings, difficulty sleeping, weight gain or loss, acne, breast swelling or tenderness, changes in sexual interest, unwanted hair growth, or hair loss. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, this medication, especially when used with an estrogen product, may rarely cause serious and potentially fatal blood clot-related problems, such as heart attack, stroke, or blood clots in the lungs, legs, or eyes. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing due to an overdose, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Before taking norethindrone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the face and skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect, so limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm the unborn baby. It also passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain medications can affect how norethindrone is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole), rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), and others. This medication may also interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. Regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while taking this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal methods. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
